newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways makes further gain on weak baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways makes further gain on weak baht.

text.p: Shares of Thai Airways International Plc extended gains into a sixth consecutive day on Tuesday as investors bought on expectations current baht weakness will see earnings rise, brokers said.
"The company's outlook is very good after the baht flotation. The baht's weakness is expected to boost its profit," one broker at Nava Finance and Securities said.
By 0834 GMT Thai Airways shares had gained 2.50 baht to 57.50 on total volume of 1.5 million shares.

Brokers said Thai Airways' revenue is mostly denominated in foreign currencies. This should help the firm post gains on foreign exchange because the baht has weakened by more than 15 percent since it was allowed to float last Wednesday.
The weaker baht may also help give the company a competitive advantage over other carriers, they said.
Thai Airways posted a 3.38 billion baht ($118.6 million) net profit in the year ended September 30, 1996, against 3.24 billion a year earlier.
